clue.text: Drawer once containing office PC?

parts.note: JOHN is slang for a toilet, which is euphemistically called 'the usual offices'
PC is short for Police Constable

explanation.surface: A desk drawer that once held an office computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is not furniture but someone who draws. 'Office' as a toilet euphemism is old British usage. 'Containing' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The English landscape painter (1776-1837) was an artist, someone who drew, and is long dead.

clue.text: What 1 used get mixed in a pot still, periodically

indicators.note: things that get mixed are stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
taking letters at regular intervals, here the odd ones of the word still

explanation.surface: Something being blended in a distillery's pot still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes SIL from 'still'; 'get mixed' shuffles that with INAPOT. A pot still is a whisky-making vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable, the painter at 1 across, worked in pigments bound with linseed or similar drying oil.

clue.text: Approaches Arsenal about wanting a midfielder

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so these letters are taken away from the club's name

parts.note: read as mid-fielder: the middle letter of 'fielder' is L

explanation.surface: A football team closing in without one of its central players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes A and L (the middle of 'fielder') from ARSENAL, leaving RSENA; 'about' rearranges it. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come close to it, a plain synonym for approach.

clue.text: Didn't include synonym for 'hand' in dictionary

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone complains a dictionary left out a word meaning 'hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out, the same as not included, in the past tense.

clue.text: Horse, one sporting queer ears more inclined to droop

indicators.note: sporting means wearing or showing, so the scrambled ears hold the other letters
queer means odd, so the letters of ears are jumbled

parts.note: GG, gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A horse with oddly shaped ears looks rather droopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' makes SAER, and 'sporting' means wearing: the horse and the one sit inside that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Saggier is the comparative of saggy, sinking or hanging down more.

clue.text: Carrying out transfer of a second new player?

parts.note: a signing is a player newly recruited to a team

explanation.surface: A football club completes a deal for another new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about transfer deadline day; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning property or rights means formally handing them over to another party.

clue.text: Left part of church in decline

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church, usually behind the altar

explanation.surface: An abandoned section of a church falling into ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a fall in standards, a slipping or deterioration.

clue.text: Heroic twin brother of princess tormenting us with We Three Kings! Really?

indicators.note: tormenting means twisting or distorting, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, three of them give KKK

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a carol being sung at them yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tormenting' rearranges US, WE, KKK and REALLY. The definition plays on the gospel names elsewhere in the grid; the hero is twin to Princess Leia in Star Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Star Wars films the Jedi hero discovers that Princess Leia is his twin sister.

clue.text: Poet that's written book on composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the book comes before the composer

parts.note: Matthew is a book of the New Testament
Malcolm Arnold was an English composer

explanation.surface: A poet who has written a book about a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's written' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer of 'Dover Beach' was also a critic, but chiefly remembered for verse.

clue.text: Removing contents of new Audi with long name

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Clearing out a new Audi that has a lengthy model name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AUDI, LONG and N together.
explanation.definitionFit: Unloading a car or lorry means taking out its cargo, so it fits 'removing contents of'.

clue.text: Reddish-brown start to autumn, in two different ways

parts.note: the phrase 'start to autumn' is read twice: once as Sep 1 (SEP plus I for one), the first of September, when autumn begins

indicators.note: start to here takes the first letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: Describing the russet colours as autumn begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to autumn' works twice: as the date Sep I, and as the opening letter of 'autumn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the brown pigment from cuttlefish ink, used of old photographs' tone.

clue.text: Last to use vehicle's a Welshman

indicators.note: last to takes the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a van is a vehicle; with the 's it gives VANS

explanation.surface: A Welshman is the last to use the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Evans is a typically Welsh surname, so stands for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Get gripes regularly: content's missing from supermarket with most small branches

parts.note: to twig is to get or understand

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the first, third and fifth of gripes
the inside of the word supermarket is removed, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A shopper complains about a supermarket's missing contents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives GIE from 'gripes'; 'content's missing from' leaves ST from 'supermarket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiggy means covered in twigs, slender shoots, so the superlative has the most of them.

clue.text: Type of spirit, sort served alongside wine

indicators.note: served alongside signals the pieces placed next to each other in sequence

parts.note: kind means sort or type
red is wine

explanation.surface: A sort of spirit drink served with wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'spirit' is not a drink but the phrase 'kindred spirit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindred spirit is a person who shares your outlook, so the word names that type.

clue.text: Rubbish prison, said dissenting voice

parts.note: refuse is rubbish

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a prison is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuseniks were Soviet Jews denied emigration; it now means anyone who refuses to comply, a dissenter.

clue.text: All but first of fires put out leading to charge, if put out again

indicators.note: leading to puts this piece before the next
put out means disturbed, so those letters are rearranged
all but the first letter of the word fires is kept

parts.note: to sue is to bring a legal charge

explanation.surface: Fires being extinguished ahead of a prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but first of' leaves IRES; 'put out' rearranges it as REIS. 'put out' recurs as the definition, in its publishing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book or record is to publish or release it once more.

clue.text: Pils drunk by nurses? Shock horror, for some

indicators.note: drunk means messed up, so the letters of Pils are jumbled

parts.note: tends means nurses or looks after

explanation.surface: Nurses horrified at someone drinking lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Pils is a pilsner lager. 'Shock' is a mass of hair, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed tips of hair are a horror to some people about their shock, or mop of hair.

clue.text: Longing for women, if lust unbridled

indicators.note: unbridled means unrestrained, so the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Desire for women when lust is unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful means full of yearning, as a longing look is.

clue.text: One searching smallest room, say, for complaint in the Observer

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the smallest room is the loo, and one searching carefully is a comber, as in beachcomber

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports someone hunting through a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Observer' looks like the newspaper but is the eye, which observes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leucoma is a white opacity of the cornea, an ailment of the eye, the organ that observes.

clue.text: Finery of sporting gear worn by boxer

indicators.note: worn by means the jumbled gear is put around the boxer
sporting means playful, so the letters of gear are rearranged

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a champion boxer

explanation.surface: Fine sports kit worn by a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial robes and emblems, grand dress.

clue.text: Prize crossword compiler needing oxygen intake after cycling

indicators.note: intake signals one letter taken in by the other piece
cycling sends a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a setter compiles crosswords
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A prize puzzle setter needing oxygen after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final R of SETTER to the front, RSETTE; O goes in after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as an award, as at shows.

clue.text: Bloomers in game against Premier League side

parts.note: a lark is a game or bit of fun
Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: Wearing underpants for a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' are not knickers but plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspurs are delphinium-like garden plants, flowering ones, so bloomers.

clue.text: Educated girl eating a yoghurt-based side dish

indicators.note: eating means the girl's name takes the letter in

parts.note: Educating Rita is a play and film, so Rita is the educated girl

explanation.surface: A schooled girl eating a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Educated girl' alludes to the play 'Educating Rita'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian accompaniment of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: Two characters going after 1 (not Turner) in shop

parts.note: Constable (1 across) was a Royal Academician, so RA follows his name

indicators.note: a turner turns something round, so the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: Seemingly about Constable and Turner, rival painters.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner is the painter Constable's rival, but here 'Turner' reverses NOT. 'Shop' is slang for informing on.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone, in British slang, is to inform on them to the police.

clue.text: Stiff, cold and unfeeling? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed

parts.note: frigid means icy cold and also emotionally unresponsive

explanation.surface: Someone stiff, cold and unfeeling, or not initially so.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means inflexible, unbending.

clue.text: Bottled water that's still the first drunk by 12 mostly

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed, so one piece goes inside the other
mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is EVANS
I is the Roman numeral for one, the first

explanation.surface: The Welshman of 12 drinks the first still water.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian is a French brand of mineral water sold uncarbonated.

clue.text: With eight sides in National League heading for administration, first month has past

indicators.note: first means the month and past come before the rest

parts.note: Oct is October
ago means past

indicators.note: in puts one letter within another pair

parts.note: NL is National League

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of administration

explanation.surface: A football league in administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagonal shapes are polygons with eight edges.

clue.text: Cyclist of note about to sell his pants

parts.note: a mark is a note
CA, circa, means about
vend means sell

indicators.note: pants, British slang for rubbish, makes the letters a mess

explanation.surface: A famous cyclist sells his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, here the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx sprinter is a record Tour de France stage winner on bikes.
